messages:
kai: hi team, first-day question  I can start the stack but the app immediately errors with `psql: FATAL: password authentication failed for user "postgres"`. I thought docker-compose was reading .env. I have a .env with POSTGRES_PASSWORD=localpass and compose has `env_file: .env` on the db service. Any quick sanity checks?

nora: welcome! quick Q: are you running the web app in a container or on your host? if on host, it might be using a different env source.

kai: running the app in a container (the web service in the same compose file). compose command is `docker-compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up --build`. db service has `environment:` commented out and only `env_file: .env`.

ben: FYI compose variable interpolation vs env_file semantics are confusing. `env_file` injects variables into the container at runtime, but compose variable substitution (like ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}) in the compose YAML is done by the shell before compose runs and reads from the environment (including a top-level .env file next to the compose file). If you have an env_file but also use ${...} earlier in the compose file, those values may not come from the same place.

kai: hmm we do use `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}` in the command/args for db init in that second compose file. so maybe the value isn't substituted. How do I check what the container actually sees?

nora: run `docker-compose exec db env | grep POSTGRES` to see env inside the container. Also `docker inspect <container> --format '{{json .Config.Env}}'` if you need raw config. If the password inside the container is empty or different, Postgres will reject the connection from the app.

ben: also check your host shell: any exported POSTGRES_PASSWORD in your environment will override .env substitution for compose. Compose picks up your shell env when doing variable interpolation. If you want deterministic behavior, ensure a top-level `.env` file exists (compose will load it for interpolation) and avoid `env_file` for substitution confusion. Another gotcha: `env_file` does not create docker secrets; it's just a file injected into the container environment.

kai: ran `docker-compose exec db env | grep POSTGRES` and it shows `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=otherpass` which I don't recognize. Where did that come from?

nora: possible sources: (1) a different .env in the directory where you ran compose, (2) an exported variable in your shell, or (3) the second compose file overriding env with a different value. Run `env | grep POSTGRES` on your host to check shell env. Also `git grep POSTGRES_PASSWORD` to find other compose files.

ben: if you changed POSTGRES_* after the DB was initialized, the existing data directory will still have the original credentials in the database cluster (Postgres only uses the env on first init). So if you re-run with a new password but the volume already exists, Postgres won't re-initialize and login will fail. To apply new creds you need to recreate the data volume (backup first) or manually alter the postgres role password with psql.

kai: ohhh I did tweak .env while iterating. I see a named volume `project_db-data` still present. So that could be it. What is the safe path to fix for local dev?

nora: safe options: 1) If you can lose dev data, `docker-compose down -v` will remove named volumes (or `docker volume rm project_db-data`), then `docker-compose up` will re-init Postgres with the current env credentials. 2) If you need data, exec into the db container and `psql -U postgres` as a superuser (if you know the old password) and `ALTER USER postgres WITH PASSWORD 'newpass';` or create a new user that your app can use. 3) Start a temporary postgres container with a fresh named volume, initialize it with the intended password, and migrate data if needed.

kai: i don't have critical dev data, so i'll recreate. one more question: app's DATABASE_URL is set via `environment` in the web service using `${DATABASE_URL}` interpolation. what if the app uses a runtime .env loader (like dotenv) inside the container? which wins?

ben: order is: compose will substitute variables in the compose file using shell env and the top-level .env; then it will set container env from `environment:` or `env_file:`. If your app loads a .env at runtime inside the container (e.g., `dotenv` reading `/app/.env`), that is entirely inside the container and can override or complement what compose injected, but only if the file exists in the container. So for predictability, either supply the final runtime env via `environment:` in compose or mount a known `/app/.env` into the container and document it.

kai: thanks, i did `docker-compose down -v`, ensured the .env in repo has POSTGRES_PASSWORD=localpass, restarted compose and `docker-compose exec db env` shows the right password. App connects now. I also added a note to my onboarding doc about not changing DB creds mid-run.

devex-bot: pinned: quick checklist for DB auth issues: 1) check env inside container `docker-compose exec db env` 2) remember compose interpolation vs env_file differences 3) volume re-init required for POSTGRES_* changes on first-run 4) use named volumes and document creds in `.env.example`. See internal guide: https://redwood.internal/dev/compose-env-and-db-credentials

kai: thanks everyone! documented steps in my notes and added `.env.example` to my fork. :sparkles:
